content.user_title: Diagnose Build Failures With Root Cause Analysis
content.value_statement: Build blockers often hide behind unclear logs, broken configuration, or incomplete tests. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through diagnosis, fix planning, validation, and escalation.
actual_capabilities: Structures build blocker investigation into reproduction, context gathering, root cause analysis, and solution planning.
Prompts agents to inspect configuration files, logs, related code, and documentation before changing code.
Guides validation with specific success criteria, rollback thinking, and before-and-after reporting.
Covers common blocker patterns including memory limits, missing directories, type mismatches, and circular dependencies.
Defines escalation criteria when the blocker cannot be reproduced or the fix needs major architecture changes.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts, automated scanners, or project-specific commands beyond examples.
Requires access to the target repository, build logs, and relevant configuration files.
Cannot guarantee a fix when the root cause needs product or architecture decisions.
May require web or documentation lookup for framework-specific build failures.

use_cases.title: Resolve CI Build Failures
use_cases.description: Investigate failing build jobs, collect logs, identify the root cause, and propose a verified fix plan.

use_cases.title: Debug Typecheck Blockers
use_cases.description: Trace TypeScript errors to changed interfaces, incorrect usage, or stale patterns before applying a minimal fix.

use_cases.title: Escalate Hard Blockers Clearly
use_cases.description: Summarize confirmed facts, failed attempts, likely causes, and decisions needed from a maintainer.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Build Investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: A build command fails and you need a structured first pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the build-diagnostics skill to investigate this build failure. Reproduce the error, collect the main logs, inspect likely configuration files, and summarize the root cause with confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Likely Root Causes
prompt_templates.scenario: Several causes seem possible and the team needs prioritization.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the build-diagnostics workflow to rank possible causes for this blocker. Explain the evidence for each cause, the missing information, and the safest next check.

prompt_templates.title: Plan and Validate a Minimal Fix
prompt_templates.scenario: The root cause is likely known and a fix needs careful validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the build-diagnostics skill to design a minimal fix. Include the current state, proposed change, risk level, validation steps, success criteria, and rollback plan.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Escalation Report
prompt_templates.scenario: The blocker cannot be solved safely without human input.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the build-diagnostics escalation format. Report what is known, what was tried, why it failed, ranked possible causes, and the exact decisions needed.

output_examples.input: A Next.js build fails because the manifest cannot be written.
output_examples.output: The report identifies the failing write step, checks configuration and output paths, proposes the most likely directory or permission cause, and lists validation steps.

output_examples.input: A typecheck job reports many related assignment errors after an interface change.
output_examples.output: The response groups the errors by changed contract, identifies affected call sites, recommends a minimal mapping fix, and defines passing typecheck as success.

output_examples.input: A test suite has missing coverage and unclear failures.
output_examples.output: The diagnosis separates missing tests from failing tests, reviews working examples, and explains whether the blocker needs implementation, scope clarification, or escalation.

best_practices: Reproduce the blocker before changing files.
Separate symptoms from the root cause and cite concrete evidence.
Verify the fix under the same conditions that produced the failure.
anti_patterns: Changing code before understanding the failure path.
Treating a passing partial check as full validation.
Escalating without facts, attempted steps, and clear decisions needed.

faq.question: What does this skill help diagnose?
faq.answer: It helps diagnose build failures, typecheck errors, test blockers, configuration problems, and unclear CI failures.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides diagnostic guidance for an agent or user to run appropriate project commands with normal approval.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It references Bash, file reading, search, documentation lookup, web search, and Playwright when those tools are available.

faq.question: Can it fix every build failure?
faq.answer: No. It helps find and validate likely fixes, but some blockers require maintainer or architecture decisions.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertainty?
faq.answer: It asks for confidence levels, alternative causes, validation plans, and escalation when evidence is incomplete.

faq.question: Is it useful for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they can inspect files and run approved checks.
